articles.title: Quad9 (DNS Resolver) to Exit France
articles.content: Back to Blog Farewell, France We have some news to share with you. Summary Starting November 24, Quad9 will no longer be able to offer its free cyberprotection service to users located in France. The French courts yesterday handed down an unfavorable ruling against Quad9 in a major case that undermines the transparency and stability of the internet. This decision in favor of beIN forces Quad9 to block the recursive DNS resolution for a number of domain names for users located in France. The good news is the court significantly reduced the financial penalty, from €580,000 to €1,000 per day. However, for Quad9, this has never been just a financial issue: it is a matter of principle. We cannot comply with this ruling over the long term while remaining faithful to our mission to protect your privacy, defend you against cyber threats, and preserve the integrity of the internet. For us, recursive DNS resolution is a neutral and passive service. We categorically refuse to alter or lie to you about the DNS responses you receive in a way that opposes your expectations. This ruling forces an untenable position upon us. Compliance is technically unfeasible, and implementation directly contradicts our mandate to serve the public. As a result, we have made the difficult decision to withdraw Quad9 services from France as of Tuesday, November 24. We deeply regret that French internet users will be left without an alternative that can adequately protect their cybersecurity while remaining compliant with European privacy law. Background beIN, a Qatari company with offices in France, previously sought to force Quad9 to block resolution for a set of domain names they assert are participating in copyright infringement of its audiovisual rights on sports event broadcasts. Quad9 has no association with these domain names, nor with the operators of the websites. The French courts have fundamentally misunderstood the working of the internet and the role of the domain name system and have allowed a financial penalty to apply to Quad9 if we do not block DNS responses to users in France. Quad9 is a Swiss public-benefit, nonprofit foundation established for the explicit purpose of protecting the cybersecurity of internet users. We charge nothing for our service and serve all people and organizations which seek to improve the security and privacy of their internet use. Our core values are to make privacy, security, and integrity available to all internet users, and our mission is to universally apply these guiding principles to recursive DNS resolution services in order to serve end users. articles.title: Jailbreaking the Switch 2
articles.content: ns2jb is a software-only jailbreak of the switch 2 for the current latest firmware 23.0.1 Introduction You can get a copy of the exploit from the ns2jb repository. ns2jb is a software-only, tethered jailbreak for the Switch 2. It allows running arbitrary native code as any ordinary sysmodule, and as the built-in fs sysmodule. This lets us run homebrew, reverse engineer and mod Switch 2 games, back up save files off the Switch, and access most of the Switch 2’s peripherals through MMIO. To my knowledge, it’s the first such exploit for the Switch 2. To demonstrate the capabilities of this jailbreak, Codex modded a Switch 2 exclusive, Mario Kart World. Thanks to my friends in Dabney House who helped me choose characters to add and playtest the game. cinnamoroll, red, and tole tole racing Setup The very first thing I did was set up a harness around the Switch 1 and 2 so Codex could, ideally, jailbreak the Switch 2 without me: “set a goal to jailbreak the switch 2. make no mistakes” Edit: Many people have been asking me if I actually used this prompt. No, it’s just a silly caption. I set a /goal for userland code execution, but that didn’t succeed. The jailbreak itself took substantial effort for ~2 weeks. The Mario Kart World, however, was entirely vibecoded in a day, and was just for fun. The JetKVMs allow Codex to send controller inputs to the Switches over USB and receive video output over HDMI. We also need a way to press the power button—when the Switch 2 crashes, it needs a button press to restart. That’s what the Bluetooth light switch flicker from Amazon is for. When the lever comes down, it presses the power button. Once the power button is fully pressed, the rest of the lever’s torque lifts the mechanism. watch the power button get pressed Getting code execution WebKit is a popular target for console jailbreaks, so it’s unsurprising that Codex has picked it for initial code execution. Code execution through the browser It claims to have “native control-flow hijack” by taking advantage of a WebKit n-day loaded via a custom Wi-Fi captive portal. We’d like to get code execution in microkernel services (or “sysmodules” on the Switch), so we can run homebrew, mod games, download saves, etc. Unfortunately, this approach of replacing one JavaScript function object with another doesn’t generalize beyond existing functions—we’d need a new way to make arbitrary IPC calls. That looks difficult. Why? WebKit has execute-only memory, or XOM, so even with arbitrary memory RW, we don’t know where a gadget that could perform arbitrary IPC calls is. Even if we did, perhaps by parsing relocation data, it’s not clear how we’d construct a signed pointer for it because of PAC. And even if we could, with some signing gadget, it’s not clear how we’d call this pointer, since CFI type-checks most call sites. Codex has reset the goal to complete these steps. It’s a side bet; it may succeed 1 , but let’s be real: the accessibility of WebKit and the Nintendo BBP reward

articles.title: OpenShell – A safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents
articles.content: Important New in OpenShell 0.1.x: a stable release cadence, new isolation primitives, an expanded extension surface, and new APIs. Read the 0.1.0 upgrade guide . OpenShell is the safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents. Agents are most useful when they can read files, install packages, call APIs, and use credentials. OpenShell gives them that capability without giving them unrestricted access to your data, secrets, or network. You declare what each agent can touch in a policy, and OpenShell enforces it. OpenShell governs what agents can do in two ways: it instruments the kernel to enforce policy on every file access, system call, and network connection at runtime, and it uses formal verification to check what a policy change would allow before it is applied. Kernel-level enforcement. Each agent runs in an isolated sandbox. Kernel controls confine which files it can access and which system calls it can make, and every network connection passes through a policy check before it leaves the sandbox. Agents never see real credentials; OpenShell adds them only to requests bound for approved endpoints. Formally verified policy changes. Before a policy change is approved, OpenShell uses formal verification to flag risky new access it would grant, such as reaching a new host with credentials or calling a new API method, so those changes wait for human review. See Architecture for how the gateway, supervisor, and sandbox fit together. You need Linux, macOS on Apple Silicon, or Windows with WSL 2 (experimental), plus Docker, Podman, or host virtualization. See the Support Matrix for details. curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell/main/install.sh | sh openshell sandbox create --name demo The installer sets up the CLI and a local gateway. The default sandbox image is minimal Ubuntu with no agent installed. To run a real agent, follow Run Your First Agent : it runs OpenCode against a free OpenRouter model and shows how to approve new access as the agent needs it. Sandboxes : images, runtimes, GPUs, and lifecycle. Policies : filesystem, network, and process rules, with the advisor and prover for reviewing changes. Providers : credentials that work only at approved endpoints, including inference . Gateways : the control plane for sandboxes, policy, and access. Kubernetes : deploy the gateway with Helm. Your CNI must enforce NetworkPolicy . Extensibility : middleware, interceptors, and compute drivers. Tutorials : step-by-step policy and agent walkthroughs. Prerelease and development builds : try an upcoming release or the latest commit on main . Install the public OpenShell skills for your coding agent: npx skills add NVIDIA/OpenShell The skills teach your agent to drive the OpenShell CLI, write sandbox policies, and debug gateways and inference routing. articles.title: Woman faces six years in prison over Cash App account she never opened
articles.content: WTF?! Digital identity fraud is far from something new, but this case shows just how extreme the repercussions can be. A Cash App account opened in someone else's name and used in scams could lead to an innocent person being sentenced to years in prison. The problem is that the company initially refused to provide information about the account because she couldn't prove that she was the owner. In April, Amanda Smith was shocked to discover officers at her upstate Pennsylvania home with a warrant for her arrest, writes 404 Media . The alleged crime took place in Arkansas – more than a thousand miles away in a state she'd never visited. Smith was taken to the local jail, where she was locked up for three nights. Her bail was initially set at $50,000, but Smith says authorities told her there was little point in paying it because they intended to extradite her to Arkansas anyway. After being released, she and her husband drove to Arkansas for a court appearance, where she was fingerprinted and photographed. Another $20,000 bail was imposed before she could return home. Smith later discovered why she had been arrested: a scammer had tricked someone into sending $1,000 to a Cash App account, one that was in her name but controlled by a criminal. It turned out that the account had been created using Smith's Social Security number and date of birth. But Smith, who describes herself as not tech-savvy, said she had never used Cash App. The situation sounds like one that should have been resolved quickly. But Smith says she is still being asked to prove her innocence in an ongoing criminal case. One stumbling block was that Cash App refused to hand over details of the account to Smith because she couldn't prove she was the owner. She eventually received the data through discovery in her case. Shockingly, Smith is now facing up to six years in prison for a crime she says she didn't commit and knew nothing about. The charges include computer fraud, unlawful use of a communication device, and theft of property. "They're trying to turn it into my problem [...] that I need to prove that I'm innocent," Smith told 404 Media. "That's not what I grew up believing was the way it worked." Not too surprisingly, the fraud took place on that bastion of honest transactions, Facebook Marketplace. The buyer found items for sale and messaged the seller, who told them to send money to his wife's Cash App account. The name on the account was Amanda Smith. Unfortunately, the seller's Facebook account had been hacked. There were no items for sale, and the Cash App account had been created just before the scam took place. Cash App records also revealed what happened to the stolen money. Just hours after the $1,000 arrived, it was divided into smaller amounts and sent to a network of other accounts. articles.title: Getting ready to operate GNU Taler in Germany
articles.content: Getting ready to operate Taler in Germany For the past three years, the NGI Taler project has worked towards the goal of making Taler legally available in the EU as an online payment system for everyday use. Today we can share that Taler Operations AG is being founded in Bochum. The new German company is going to operate Taler in Euro, enabling payments with Taler first in Germany, then in the Euro-zone. The next steps towards that goal are to apply to BaFin, Germany's financial supervisory authority, for a licence as an e-money issuer. This post explains why this company is needed, what changed in the NGI TALER consortium, and how citizens who want to see Taler succeed can help, including as investors. Why Taler needs a regulated operator Taler is a payment system, not a currency, but usable for any currency. At its core, it issues bearer tokens to represent value, like coins, and this renders Taler as electronic money which falls under EU regulation: Any institution that issues electronic money (EMI) for Euros must be a bank or acquire a dedicated licence. In the original plan of the NGI TALER project, the Bochum-based GLS Bank took on the role of the e-money issuer for Taler, and worked towards the deployment of the Taler payment system in Germany with support from the other members of the NGI TALER consortium. However, in January 2026 GLS made the decision to not pursue this role further, for reasons unrelated to Taler as presented in their statement ( gls.de/taler ). Since then, GLS and the other members of the NGI TALER consortium worked out the best way forward to achieve the project's goal to make Taler available in the Euro-zone. The outcome is the announcement today. The new company Taler Operations AG will be set up to apply for an e-money licence and take over the role originally intended for GLS (who will remain a consortium member in a supporting role). We regret that the original plan did not work out. Integrating a new kind of payment system into an existing bank’s processes, compliance framework and IT is hard, and banks have to set priorities. We are grateful to GLS for its work in the project and for staying involved. And we also think the new arrangement has a real advantage: the institution operating Taler in Euro will be focused entirely on Taler, instead of fitting it into a larger bank’s product portfolio and process constraints. What Taler Operations AG will do Legal status: Taler Operations AG is a German stock corporation in formation, seated in Bochum, and a subsidiary of Taler Systems SA (Luxembourg). Purpose: Operating a GNU Taler exchange in Germany, for the Euro, so that citizens can pay with Taler and merchants can accept it. Reach: After establishing legal operations in Germany, Taler will become usable across the single market, even if Taler Operations AG will initially only promote it in Germany. articles.title: Run full iOS 16.5 firmware on Android Devices
articles.content: HackiOS boots Apple's open-source XNU kernel ( xnu-8796.121.2 , the kernel of iOS 16.5) on Android phone hardware and runs the unmodified iOS 16.5 user space on top of it: launchd → backboardd → SpringBoard → apps. Our own EFI loader, our own replacements for Apple's closed drivers, a UEFI port, and a Linux Wi-Fi driver on a compatibility layer make that possible. It runs in two places: POCO X5 Pro 5G (redwood, Snapdragon 778G) — nothing is flashed: the UEFI is started with fastboot boot , the whole system lives in RAM, and after a reboot the phone is back in Android; QEMU ( virt , aarch64) — the same thing on any Linux computer, no phone needed. articles.title: Hedra is a 3D open world game I wrote from scratch while in highschool
articles.content: Project Hedra is an ambitious open-world, low-poly RPG. Choose your class, explore endless procedurally generated worlds, unlock different skills and complete procedurally generated quests. More screenshots at ( Screenshots ) I started this project when I was in highschool (around 15 yo) in order to learn how OpenGL worked. The scope creep quickly arrived and after a few years it turned into a fullfledged 3D game and game engine. The codebase has around 100k LOC and the game has first class support for Linux and Windows. The million lines of code are not in vain. The game and engine are both full of features :) Beatiful procedurally generated worlds Quests and bosses 100+ items with rarities system Skills and skill tree system with N+ skills 4 different classes with 2 specializations each () Procedurally placed structures generated dynamically Fishing, crafting, etc Trading and NPCs Companions and pets Beatiful soundtrack Navigation, maps Different dimensions More stuff I don't recall :) Fully fledged renderer using modern OpenGL Skinned mesh rendering Support for loading and playing generic animations Collada (.dae) parser Static mesh rendering Screen space reflections Screen space ambient occlusion Bloom, FXAA & MSAA Modding support CI for automatically deploying to a Steam beta branch Localization support Sound support using OpenAL Python scripting support Module system for loading data oriented objects Steam integration Fully fledged UI & controls system (dropdowns, buttons, etc.) written from raw OpenGL Dynamic shader system for reloading during runtime Frustum culling, occlusion culling, Mesh simplification for runtime level of detail (LOD) Skybox support Shadows 3D trails renderering support Particle system using object instancing in opengl bulletphysics integration Chunk system for infinite worlds support .ply parsing support Dynamic meshing support using MarchingCubes Custom implementation of basic C# primitives and allocators (like Lists) for supporting stack allocated lists and minimizing the automatic runtime allocations (and thus the GC). 1000+ plus test cases Framework for mocking game components and doing integration testing on games Image and asset compression for faster loading and smaller size Entity component system More stuff I don't recall :) WorldRenderer.cs . Renders the entire world in just 3 (actually it depends on how partitioned is the data buffer, but it was designed to be in 3) draw calls (water, terrain, instanced) using glMultiDrawElements. Block.cs . Core component of the world. Read more at https://maxilevi.com/blog/procedural-meshing-hedra Fishing.py . Written in Python as a mod script using IronPython, directly interacts with the C# API. NativeArray.cs Implementation of an array primitive using a custom allocator. The same project provides heap based allocators as well as stac based ones using stackalloc . The idea was to minimize the automatic heap allocations (and thus avoiding the GC) during the game frames.

articles.title: eMudhra to exit global SSL/TLS certificate business
articles.content: Will Sharpen Focus on Core Enterprise Solutions and trust services other than SSL/TLS BENGALURU, INDIA, October 22, 2026 - eMudhra Limited (BSE: 543533 | NSE: EMUDHRA), a global digital trust company, today announced that its Board has decided to voluntarily withdraw from the global SSL/TLS certificate business. Mr. V. Srinivasan, Chairman, eMudhra Limited referred to the recent incident relating to its global SSL/TLS certificate and indicated that eMudhra handled the recent incident diligently, revoking the affected CAs within 14 hours of discovery and disclosing promptly. There were no end entity certificates issued out of the affected CA’s. Its infrastructure was not compromised and no data was breached. All physical and logical security controls remained intact. He added that global SSL/TLS is a small part of eMudhra’s business contributing to about 1% of the global revenue. Due to increasing data sovereignty & compliance requirements, complexity and cost associated with this business is increasing over the years. This, paired with the fact that some of the large entities issue the SSL/TLS free of cost, the business potential and RoI of this line of business also has considerably reduced for eMudhra when measured against our cumulative revenue base. However, the level of social media amplification around this incident has brought scrutiny that is out of proportion to SSL/TLS’s place in our business. In view of this, after detailed deliberations our board has concluded that withdrawing from global SSL/TLS is the right decision for eMudhra and its shareholders. For many certifying authorities, SSL/TLS is the whole business. For eMudhra it is one part of a much broader digital solutions portfolio. We will put our energy where we create the most value for customers with Sharpened Focus on Core Enterprise Solutions and trust services other than SSL/TLS. Seamless transition for customers Our G1 RSA roots will continue to serve customers until this transition is complete as we work with browser programs and our customers to enable this transition. eMudhra will reach out to affected customers to replace any certificate free of cost from partners through the transition. Core businesses unaffected eMudhra’s global SSL/TLS infrastructure runs separately from its other operations. articles.title: Firefox Local Mode

articles.content: I often find myself writing (by which I mean generating) functions to convert enums to strings. A naïve implementation of such a function might look like: const char * dxgi_format_to_string( unsigned x) { switch (x) { case 0 : return "UNKNOWN" ; case 1 : return "R32G32B32A32_TYPELESS" ; case 2 : return "R32G32B32A32_FLOAT" ; case 3 : return "R32G32B32A32_UINT" ; case 4 : return "R32G32B32A32_SINT" ; case 5 : return "R32G32B32_TYPELESS" ; case 6 : return "R32G32B32_FLOAT" ; case 7 : return "R32G32B32_UINT" ; case 8 : return "R32G32B32_SINT" ; case 9 : return "R16G16B16A16_TYPELESS" ; case 10 : return "R16G16B16A16_FLOAT" ; case 11 : return "R16G16B16A16_UNORM" ; case 12 : return "R16G16B16A16_UINT" ; case 13 : return "R16G16B16A16_SNORM" ; case 14 : return "R16G16B16A16_SINT" ; case 15 : return "R32G32_TYPELESS" ; case 16 : return "R32G32_FLOAT" ; case 17 : return "R32G32_UINT" ; case 18 : return "R32G32_SINT" ; case 19 : return "R32G8X24_TYPELESS" ; case 20 : return "D32_FLOAT_S8X24_UINT" ; case 21 : return "R32_FLOAT_X8X24_TYPELESS" ; case 22 : return "X32_TYPELESS_G8X24_UINT" ; default : return NULL; } } Compiling the above with a modern gcc at -O0 or -O1 gives some fairly horrible assembly code. Thankfully, at -O2 and above, a modern gcc can rewrite it to something more along the lines of: const char * dxgi_format_to_string( unsigned x) { static const char * const cases[] = { "UNKNOWN" , "R32G32B32A32_TYPELESS" , "R32G32B32A32_FLOAT" , "R32G32B32A32_UINT" , "R32G32B32A32_SINT" , "R32G32B32_TYPELESS" , "R32G32B32_FLOAT" , "R32G32B32_UINT" , "R32G32B32_SINT" , "R16G16B16A16_TYPELESS" , "R16G16B16A16_FLOAT" , "R16G16B16A16_UNORM" , "R16G16B16A16_UINT" , "R16G16B16A16_SNORM" , "R16G16B16A16_SINT" , "R32G32_TYPELESS" , "R32G32_FLOAT" , "R32G32_UINT" , "R32G32_SINT" , "R32G8X24_TYPELESS" , "D32_FLOAT_S8X24_UINT" , "R32_FLOAT_X8X24_TYPELESS" , "X32_TYPELESS_G8X24_UINT" , }; if (x > 22u ) return NULL; return cases[x]; } The assembly code for this is much nicer, although the table of pointers still takes up more space than I'd like (and that's before you account for each table entry needing a relocation entry...). articles.title: Google's Rust Style Guide
articles.content: Rust Style Guide This document is a style guide for the usage of the Rust programming language at Google. In this context, “style” refers to more than just formatting; it includes guidance on API and implementation design. Rust is used in many places, including google3 , Android, ChromeOS, Fuchsia, and Chrome, and we’d like for Rust usage at Google to be consistent both within and across codebases. In addition to bringing consistency to our Rust code, style guidance also helps establish a standard of quality. Background Scope The current scope of authority of the rules outlined in this guide: In Android, Chromium, and other codebases : This style guide has been developed in consultation with other codebases, and they intend to start applying it. These codebases may have their own rules about how strictly this is expected to be applied. Expect more information here as these codebases adopt this guide. Goals of the style guide By and large, we have this document for the same reasons we have a C++ style guide . Most style rules come from one or more of the goals listed below. Style rules should prioritize readability and maintainability over writeability We expect our code to be around for long periods of time, and we consider a little bit of extra effort applied during code writing to be worth it in the long run if the style rule improves readability. Style rules should favor better automation Large-Scale Changes (LSCs) are common at Google, and consistency helps make LSCs easier to carry out. Style rules should be consistent with the wider Rust ecosystem where possible The broader Rust ecosystem already has a pretty good amount of consistency in style, and we should rely on that where possible to reduce surprise and make it less work to learn Google’s Rust style. Style rules should pull their weight Every Rust developer and reviewer at Google has to keep these style rules in mind: as such, we should be careful to include rules that have a tangible benefit. Style rules may help avoid minor style disagreements There are many cases where reasonable people may disagree about a style, and we expect that disagreement to show up often on CLs. Having a style rule helps avoid having to rehash this each time. Rules in this category that do not have other benefits should be kept to a minimum. Follow public Rust style rules Follow the official public Rust style rules to the extent they don’t conflict with this style guide. A “conflict” would be a case where this style guide suggests a pattern that is discouraged, or counter to the primary encouraged pattern in the Rust style guide. Why does the guidance in this style guide deviate from regular Rust style rules? Most style guides have three goals: consistency, readability, and encouraging good API design. Regardless of the specific choices made, it helps everyone to have these choices made beforehand to limit bikeshedding. We showcased many of the new features in “A Preview of DuckDB v2.0” , which covers each one in more depth. For the complete release notes, see the release page on GitHub . articles.title: Expose only share links of a private service with caddy
articles.content: 1. Introduction § In my self-hosted infrastructure, most services are only reachable through my VPN. But some of them have a feature to share something with people outside: Immich has share links for albums and photos, Nextcloud has share links for files and folders. My self-hosted infrastructure with Incus OS I wanted to add some extra security, but the people receiving a link should not have to install a VPN client or create an account, they must be able to click on it and see the content. The usual way to do this is to expose the whole service on the Internet, and then you have to trust the login page, the API and every route of the application. I found a simple pattern with the reverse proxy caddy that only lets in requests carrying a valid share link, and answers a 404 to everything else. The service itself is used to check if the link is valid. caddy official website In this blog post, you will learn how to use caddy to expose only the "share link" part of a service, how it works, and what it brings for security. 2. The idea: forward authentication § caddy has a directive named forward_auth . Before forwarding a request to the service, caddy sends a first request to another server (the "auth server"), and looks at the answer. If the answer is a success, the real request is forwarded, otherwise caddy returns the answer of the auth server to the client. This is usually used with software like Keycloak + oauth-proxy, to add a login page in front of an application. caddy documentation: forward_auth directive Here, the auth server is the service itself. Most applications have a route answering differently if a share key is valid or not, so we can ask the application "is this link valid?" before letting the request in. The forward_auth directive is actually a shortcut for a reverse_proxy with a few options. I did not use forward_auth directly because I needed to rewrite the URL of the check request and to accept another status code than 2xx, so I wrote the long form with reverse_proxy and handle_response . This is also easier to understand, because everything is visible in the configuration. caddy documentation: reverse_proxy, intercepting responses The whole design is: the full service is reachable only through the VPN (or with an IP restriction), on a separate caddy instance (a single caddy server could work, but be sure to put IP restrictions on the internal vhost) a public caddy site exposes only the routes needed by a guest, matched very strictly for each request, caddy asks the service if the share key in the URL is valid if it is valid, the request is forwarded, if not, caddy answers 404 every other URL gets the same 404, so a visitor cannot even know which software is behind 3. articles.title: Tell your network to explain itself and then some
articles.content: Tell your network to explain itself and then some Published on 2026-10-22 . The other day I read this blog post about using arp-scan to list every device on the network in order to keep better track of devices and that's great, but we can go even further. The blog post I am talking about is Ben Calderon's post called ARP! Tell your network to explain itself . I too have too many devices on my network to keep track (it both serve some of my homelab stuff and some of my office stuff) and as such, I have used different approaches over the years. One of the early things I did was to give each device a meaningful hostname. Like "johnslaptop", "janesdesktop", "webserver", "storageserver", etc. But as you probably know, this quickly becomes problematic when you get more machines that does the same, so "webserver" turns into "oldwebserver" or you use "webserver1" and "webserver2" and then forget which is actually which. Also, when machines change hands, you have to rename them so "johnslaptop" now becomes "alexlaptop", etc. A better approach is to use a naming convention. This is especially useful if you run a large network with many devices, then you can use a scheme like "region.location.devicetype.unitnumber". On the homelab many people choose character names from one of their favorite movies or TV shows and use those as hostnames, like "homer", "marge", "bart", etc. The benefit of character names is that the name doesn't need to change if the device is used for something else or it changes hands. But the downside is that now it's even more difficult to remember what device does what. Also, in both cases, you cannot remember what IP address belongs to what machine. Using arp-scan in order to take advantage of the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) is a great way to determine which IPv4 devices are up and running on your network and it's much faster than scanning with nmap. $ $ arp-scan 192.168.1.0/24 Interface: eth0, type: EN10MB, MAC: 1g:36:4f:16:a2:3a, IPv4: 192.168.1.5 Starting arp-scan 1.10.0 with 256 hosts (https://github.com/royhills/arp-scan) ... 192.168.1.5 b0:56:9a:e1:66:b9 Intel Corporate 192.168.1.12 1a:83:04:16:d4:a3 (Unknown) 192.168.1.23 30:ab:d6:d2:b3:36 ASUSTek COMPUTER INC. ... 15 packets received by filter, 0 packets dropped by kernel Ending arp-scan 1.10.0: 256 hosts scanned in 2.018 seconds (126.86 hosts/sec). 15 responded If you're using IPv6 then arp-scan will not work as IPv6 uses Neighbor Discovery Protocol (NDP) rather than ARP, but I am sure you already know this if you have implemented IPv6 in your network. In the above result from arp-scan we get the IP address, the MAC address and sometimes, but only sometimes, the vendor of the NIC. Still, this is only really useful to tell me which devices are up and running, from the above I cannot determine what is what. Especially with the 192.168.1.12 one which doesn't list the vendor. articles.title: Objects, attributes, maps, oh my
articles.content: Or, IC UC we all C for ICs . In many dynamically typed programming languages, objects look like a big ol’ mapping of names to values. The languages encourage this flexibility. Consider for example Python: class C : def __init__ ( self ): self . a = 1 self . b = 2 Or Ruby: class C def initialize @a = 1 @b = 2 end end Or JavaScript : let obj = {}; obj . a = 1 ; obj . b = 2 ; This might encourage the VM implementor to model object attributes using a hash table. Hash tables, after all, are very good at mapping names to values. Here is, by way of example, a Python sketch of what this object model looks like. Because it is a sketch, it uses write_attr and read_attr instead of the much more common syntax that your programming language comes with. MISSING = object () class Instance : def __init__ ( self ): # TODO: the rest of your object system self . cls = ... self . _fields = {} def read_attr ( self , fieldname ): return self . _fields . get ( fieldname , MISSING ) def write_attr ( self , fieldname , value ): self . _fields [ fieldname ] = value obj = Instance () obj . write_attr ( "a" , 1 ) obj . write_attr ( "b" , 2 ) print ( obj . read_attr ( "a" ) + obj . read_attr ( "b" )) This has its benefits: it is straightforward to understand … uh, well, maybe that’s it. It also has its drawbacks: it uses a hash table for a very common operation: while this is technically O(1), hashing and probing are very slow it has an indirection: jumping from an object to its separate hash table field storage requires a lot of dependent memory loads. object attributes are accessed frequently and should therefore be stored in-line on the object instead of another memory access (and potentially cache miss) away This is a pretty good case where the hash table doesn't have its own internal fragmentation. This means that literally every operation a.b is doing hundreds or thousands of CPU instructions, including multiple dependent memory loads. This is not good for performance. So runtime implementors tend to implement this thing called maps, or layouts, or shapes, or hidden classes, or structures, or probably a secret sixth name I don’t know about, which optimizes reading, writing, and storage of attributes. But what does this shape code look like? How does it actually help performance? A lot of big production runtimes have pretty hairy code with domain-specific edge cases so they may not help get a handle on the basics. And a lot of blog posts, while excellent high-level overviews, are lacking in implementation. So here we go once more, blogging where everyone else has already blogged before. articles.title: I built a garbage collector for Rust (2023)
articles.content: If carcinization happens when languages evolve to be more like Rust, then what do you call it when Rust evolves to be more like Java? Caffeination? Over this summer, I’ve had a decent amount of time to kill. What better way to spend a beautiful hot summer than sitting inside, staring at core dumps in a supposedly memory-safe language? I built a garbage collector - in short, a piece of software that manages allocations for another, more exciting piece of software. The cool part: I made it in Rust, for Rust - a language designed to eliminate garbage collection and which provides few facilities for making it work properly. Not only that, I managed to make my garbage collector work with relatively few compromises, which I’ll describe in further detail lower down. If you don’t like reading, don’t care about the journey to implement it, or just want to get a sales pitch for the final result, check out the source code on GitHub here . You can also download it directly from crates.io . Background If you’re familiar with the details of Rust and its standard library, feel free to skip this section. The core backing behind Rust’s memory model is affine typing and the borrow checker . Values may only be bound to one identifier at a time, and borrows (a.k.a. references) may not outlive the scope binding their referent. For example, the following code is invalid: let x = vec! [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] ; let y = x ; println! ( " { x:? } " ) ; // compile error - x has already been moved Normally, we work around this by borrowing against a binding, such as by making y = &x in the example above. However, we often need to share some heap-allocated value without knowing which binding will live the longest. The solution to this problem is shared ownership via garbage collection. Rust’s standard library offers two simple reference-counted garbage collectors: the single-threaded Rc and its atomically-indexed counterpart Arc . They operate by maintaining a reference count in each heap allocation. Under most circumstances, these work great, but they can’t handle cyclic references. Combined with interior mutability, it’s trivial to refute them. use std :: { cell :: OnceCell , rc :: Rc } ; struct Foo ( OnceCell < Rc < Foo > > ) ; let x = Rc :: new ( Foo ( OnceCell :: new ( ) ) ) ; x . 0 . set ( Rc :: clone ( & x ) ) ; // My foo has a reference to itself. It can never be freed! This is why people actually get paid money to build garbage collectors. If using a reference counter were all you needed, a number of people working at Oracle would be out of a job. articles.content: I wanted to create a script that would read the verbatim content of my articles out loud to me with a synthesised voice. 1 This is entirely separate from the recent ai narration experiment. Reading the article out loud is one of my self-editing steps, to detect flow problems and awkward phrasings. I’ve discovered that hearing someone else read the article is slightly more effective than reading it out loud myself, though both are useful. When I read it out loud myself, I tend to read what I intended to say, not the words that are actually on the page. One of the more convenient ways to do this is with Python, where I’ve heard good things about Trafilatura for extracting the contents out of a web page, filtering on types of content, etc. But Trafilatura is a third-party Python dependency. Those suck because they break your scripts when you so much as glance sideways at pip . The code also ended up depending on aplay , which is a system dependency, making it two different sources of future breakage. A couple of years ago, I would probably have judged that to be too much maintenance, so I wouldn’t have created the script. Fortunately, now I know about Nix. I imagine that of those reading this article, a small crowd starts murmuring about uv . From what I understand, uv does take a lot of the headache out of managing Python dependencies. 4 I don’t know, honestly. It came around after I stopped working professionally with Python, so learning and understanding it would happen in my limited spare time, and now that I have Nix, I think I have better things to learn and understand. But it is only for Python. Nix works for any dependency, with any language. If we have an R script we want to manage the dependencies for, we’d do the exact same thing and use writeRscriptBin instead. Fast, flexible and pragmatic, PHP powers everything from your blog to the most popular websites in the world. After extracting the archive the *.exe files are ready to use. For other systems, see the installation chapter . For Windows, see Build your own PHP on Windows . For a minimal PHP build from Git, you will need autoconf, bison, and re2c. For a default build, you will additionally need libxml2 and libsqlite3. On Ubuntu, you can install these using: sudo apt install -y pkg-config build-essential autoconf bison re2c libxml2-dev libsqlite3-dev On Fedora, you can install these using: sudo dnf install re2c bison autoconf make ccache libxml2-devel sqlite-devel On MacOS, you can install these using brew : brew install autoconf bison re2c libiconv libxml2 sqlite or with MacPorts : sudo port install autoconf bison re2c libiconv libxml2 sqlite3 Generate configure: Configure your build. --enable-debug is recommended for development, see ./configure --help for a full list of options. # For development ./configure --enable-debug # For production ./configure Build PHP. Tests run in parallel by default, using up to 10 detected logical processors. Set -jN in TEST_PHP_ARGS or TESTS to override the worker count: make TEST_PHP_ARGS=-j4 test This runs make test with a maximum of 4 concurrent jobs. Alternatively, use -j1 to run tests sequentially. Additional extensions can be found on the PIE Extensions list, and installed with 🥧 PIE, the PHP Installer for Extensions or the deprecated PHP Extension Community Library - PECL . The PHP source code is located in the Git repository at github.com/php/php-src . Contributions are most welcome by forking the repository and sending a pull request. articles.title: Anthropic Takes On Muse With Claude Duet
articles.content: Anthropic has launched Claude Duet, an AI agent aimed at professionals and small businesses that competes with Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots. Here's Anthropic's description of what it can do: Each morning, it sends you a short brief on the most important items across your connected apps. Throughout the day, it keeps tabs on those apps and messages you only when something needs your attention. You can also hand it tasks of all shapes -- from simple administrative tasks of scheduling meetings to more complex ones, such as building dashboards with dozens of tools, creating financial or sales forecasts, prototyping, and building web apps. The Verge reports: Claude Duet pulls in memory, skills, and connected apps from Claude, and it has a virtual machine with a browser that it can use for completing work. Before any big step, like sending a payment or deleting something, Claude Duet messages you for approval. Given that Duet may be taking action on sensitive information, it has a new "new dedicated classifier and safety system prompt" that are "designed to reject requests to share the strictest tier of information," such as credit card numbers. Anthropic says Claude Duet is currently an "early version" and that it "still might misread a thread or miscalibrate what's urgent." It's also not "as strong" at personal errands like booking tickets. Read more of this story at Slashdot.
articles.summary: Anthropic推出面向专业人士和小企业的AI代理Claude Duet，与Meta Muse和OpenAI Dots竞争。

articles.title: To Make Way For Data Centers, Google Will Pay Others to Use Less Power
articles.content: Google is funding one of the nation's largest "virtual power plants," paying homes and businesses indirectly to reduce electricity consumption during periods of peak demand so more grid capacity can be available for data centers. Under its expanded deal with Voltus, the program could provide up to 1,070 megawatts in the Mid-Atlantic PJM grid -- roughly the output of a large nuclear reactor. The New York Times reports: That electricity won't come from new power plants. Instead, Voltus will sign up homes and businesses and give them financial incentives to curb their usage when local power demand is high or the grid is strained. Many of these reductions could occur automatically, such as through smart thermostats that dial back air-conditioning during peak summer hours or batteries that can provide temporary on-site power. Each of these tweaks frees up only a small amount of power on its own. But by aggregating them across thousands of businesses and homes, Voltus says it can reliably provide lots of extra capacity when it's most needed, and do so within a few years. While tech companies will likely ultimately need to build traditional power plants if they want to keep building large data centers, this approach could be a faster, cheaper and less-polluting option in the interim. "We really see virtual power plants as a critical short-term solution," said Ellen Zuckerman, head of energy market development for North and South America at Google. "It's a way to invest in our communities, really double down on our clean energy ambition, but also meet capacity at speed and scale." Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Microsoft Says October Updates Didn't Actually Fix VPN Issues
articles.content: joshuark shares a report from BleepingComputer: Microsoft says it mistakenly flagged a bug causing Always On VPN connection issues as fixed in the October 2026 Windows 11 cumulative updates. Always On VPN replaced the legacy DirectAccess technology and supports domain-joined, non-domain-joined, and Microsoft Entra ID-joined devices running Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server. It runs in the background and establishes secure tunnels back to the user's corporate network whenever their device connects to the internet. Microsoft first acknowledged the issue in a service alert sent to IT administrators in late September, saying it was triggered on systems running Windows 11 24H2 and later after installing the September 2026 security updates when the initial Always On VPN connection failed (e.g., when using automatic protocol selection with IKEv2 and SSTP). "When automatic protocol selection or protocol fallback was configured, affected VPN connections could remain stuck in a Connecting state or fail to connect after an initial connection attempt failed," it said. "In some cases, subsequent connection attempts could display the error, 'The specified port is already in use.'" After releasing the October 2026 Patch Tuesday Windows 11 cumulative updates, Microsoft marked the bug as resolved, but in a Tuesday update it said the issues weren't actually addressed and that a fix would ship later. "This disclosure was mistakenly updated to Resolved status on October 13, 2026. We have returned its status to Mitigated," it said in a service alert sent to IT admins. "A resolution for this issue is planned to be included in an update to be released in the coming weeks. We apologize for any inconvenience or confusion." While Microsoft continues working on a permanent solution, it shared a temporary fix that requires affected customers to choose one of two VPN tunneling protocols to work around the issue. Read more of this story at Slashdot.
articles.summary: 微软承认误将Always On VPN问题标记为已修复，10月Windows 11累积更新实际未解决该问题。

articles.title: Moderna Shares Plunge After Leak of Cancer Vaccine Data
articles.content: Moderna shares plunged as much as 25% after partial clinical trial data leaked for its personalized cancer vaccine developed with Merck, despite the full results showing promising outcomes for melanoma patients. Analysts attribute the selloff largely to inflated investor expectations rather than disappointing clinical results. CNBC reports: The personalized vaccine, known as intismeran autogene, paired with Merck's immunotherapy Keytruda reduced the risk of recurrence or death in certain melanoma patients by 42% compared with Keytruda alone. The data also showed the shot along with Keytruda reduced the risk of cancer spreading to distant parts of the body or death by 38%, compared with just the immunotherapy. The companies say about 82% of patients who received the personalized cancer vaccine alongside Keytruda were alive without their melanoma returning at two years, compared with 70% of those who received Keytruda alone. [...] Investors see the targeted vaccine as a possible breakthrough treatment, with the potential to be used in other forms of cancer in the future. It could also offer Moderna a critical additional commercial product in its pipeline, following vaccines for Covid-19, the flu and respiratory syncytial virus. "We assert this relative reduction in recurrence/death is clinically meaningful," said BMO Capital Markets analyst Evan Seigerman. "Such a reaction likely reflects inflated expectations into the full data release, rather than a true indictment on the efficacy of the combo therapy." UBS analysts said "this is overall a strong data set" and gives more confidence in upcoming studies of the vaccine in kidney and bladder cancers. They added the stock reaction may be due more to massive expectations than disappointing data. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Bose Is Buying Skullcandy
articles.content: An anonymous reader quotes a report from Wired: Longtime audio giant Bose announced on Wednesday that it's acquiring Skullcandy, the lifestyle brand known for its bass-heavy headphones. Skullcandy will remain a separate company within Bose's Premium Consumer Audio business and will still be based in Park City, Utah. The acquisition isn't out of left field. Bose has lent its audio expertise to Skullcandy over the past year under its Sound by Bose licensing program. Skullcandy designs the headphones and then works with Bose on the audio front. The relationship began with the Skullcandy Method 360 ANC earbuds in 2025 and more recently, with the Crusher 1080 ANC headphones in July. [...] This is hardly Bose's first audio acquisition (though it may be the most mainstream). Bose acquired McIntosh Group, owners of luxury audio brands McIntosh Laboratory and Sonus Faber, back in 2024. But Bose seems to be after Skullcandy's connection to its community. "What does the brand stand for? Does it have meaning for consumers? Is it relevant to a group of consumers that, frankly, we otherwise aren't reaching?" Bose CEO Lila Snyder tells WIRED. "If you think about McIntosh, Sonus Faber, and Skullcandy, they all fit into that realm. Skullcandy gives us access to a customer base that we think we're largely missing with the Bose brand." That's why Bose has no plans to relocate Skullcandy from Park City, Utah, which Snyder says is the epicenter of board sports culture. "We want to make sure we're right at the heart of it, as they always have been," she says. Skullcandy products are also affordable, especially compared to other Bose products and Bose-owned brands, which lets Bose compete at both ends of the market. Read more of this story at Slashdot.
articles.summary: Bose宣布收购以重低音耳机闻名的Skullcandy，后者将作为独立公司保留在Bose消费音频业务下。

articles.title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP Is the Cyber Equivalent of an Unexploded Bomb
articles.content: BBC technology editor Zoe Kleinman likens the recently discovered PHP security vulnerabilities to an unexploded bomb, writing, "The PHP story feels like the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb -- I have never seen such a dramatic, public and global response to a cyber event that hasn't happened yet." Although no successful attacks have been confirmed, the AI-assisted discovery of long-hidden flaws has triggered a worldwide security scramble, with websites taken offline as a precaution and administrators racing to deploy patches before attackers can exploit the vulnerabilities. From the report: The weaknesses found in the PHP programming language, which is used by millions of websites, had been quietly resting there for years and are not easy to exploit. One cyber security researcher told me he'd been up all night trying to do it as an experiment, but it was proving very difficult. [...] It was supposed to be kept quiet until everyone had a chance to fix their sites -- but the news was leaked. From that point the clock started ticking. As I write this, there are no reports that anyone or anything has succeeded in using the flaws to attack a site. "There's a real dilemma," said Prof Alan Woodward from Surrey University. "How do you alert people they need to be ready, and then that a patch is urgently required, whilst not alerting attackers? Basically you're telling everyone about the problem at the same time and hoping the defenders aren't awake enough to act as soon as the patch is out." But we do know from large web companies like Cloudflare and Palo Alto Networks that millions of attempts have been made. We probably won't know for a while whether it has worked for any criminals, because the companies affected might not be aware yet either. As far as we know the unexploded bomb remains intact for now, and for some experts this is a success. articles.title: Several Linux Kernel Vulnerabilities Accidentally Posted To Public Kernel Mailing List
articles.content: Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative appears to have accidentally disclosed several unpatched Linux kernel vulnerabilities on the public LKML instead of the private security list, including two CVSS 9.0 flaws that could enable remote code execution through SMB Direct and KSMBD. "This seemingly was a mistake with Linux's second-in-command Greg Kroah-Hartman responding to each report asking about their submission to the public mailing list," adds Phoronix. The newly-disclosed vulnerabilities include: ZDI-CAN-33549 as a CVSS 9.0 scored vulnerability for SMB Direct remote code execution vulnerability due to integer underflow. For this one there is a patch in a Git branch of code intended for Linux v7.5 but now presumably will be expedited for getting to mainline. ZDI-CAN-33774 as a KSMBD race condition that can lead to remote code execution. Another CVSS 9.0 rated vulnerability. ZDI-CAN-33367 is a vulneravbility for skbuff skb_zerocopy in the network code that can lead to local privilege escalation. For this one Linux kernel developers received a security report from another source last week over the same issue and a patch is expected to be posted soon. ZDI-CAN-34068 as a VMWGFX VMware graphics driver bug with an out-of-bounds write leading to local privilege escalation. ZDI-CAN-34076 an uninitialized resource in the NVMET code leading to information disclosure. ZDI-CAN-32005 was also posted to the mailing list a day prior for a search-domain TCP query stack buffer overflow leading to local privilege escalation. Read more of this story at Slashdot.
articles.summary: 趋势科技ZDI误将多个未修复Linux内核漏洞发到公开邮件列表，含两个可远程执行代码的9.0级漏洞。

articles.title: Repo-Atlas - Any GitHub user’s work, mapped and clustered, with stale favorites flagged.
articles.content: Type a GitHub username, get the map of what they've actually built: repos clustered by topic, stars over time, and the popular-but-stale ones flagged. Live: https://evoluteur.github.io/repo-atlas/ · permalink per user: ?u=<username> The map. Every public repo as a disc (area ∝ stars), grouped into regions of repos that share topics. Hover for details, click to open the repo. Groups by stars. The legend ranks the regions by the stars they hold, so you see where the attention actually sits. Needs attention. Repos people clearly wanted (stars in the account's top fifth, and at least 10) that are idle for over a year, archived, or built on a stack few people start with today (jQuery, AngularJS, Backbone, Bower…). Heavily forked ones get a hint that the forks may hold fixes. Stars over time. Without a token: stars held today, stacked by the year each repo was born. With a token: real cumulative star history per group, from stargazer dates. Share. A 1200×630 card for social posts and a permalink. Each repo's topics are normalised (plurals folded, generic tags like javascript , svg , ui dropped) and hyphenated topics also contribute their parts ( sacred-geometry → sacred , geometry ). Tokens are weighted by inverse document frequency across the account. Tokens used once, or by more than 45% of repos, carry no signal and are dropped. Repos with almost no topics fall back to description words. Repos are compared by cosine similarity and merged bottom-up (average linkage) until no two groups are more than 0.16 alike. The eight groups holding the most stars get a color and a two-word name (the tokens most frequent inside the group and rarest outside it). Everything else folds into loners . All of this is in src/atlas.js : pure functions, no DOM, tested with node --test . Everything runs in the browser against the public GitHub REST API. The map and the attention list work anonymously (60 requests/hour per IP; a typical account takes 2). GitHub only lists when each star was given to authenticated callers, so the star-history chart needs a token. A fine-grained token with no extra permissions is enough. It is kept in sessionStorage for the tab and only sent to api.github.com . Big repos are sampled: every stargazer page for repos under 500 stars, otherwise the first, last and three evenly spaced pages. Each fetched star is an exact (count, date) point; months in between are interpolated. Results are cached in localStorage (repos 1 hour, star history 24 hours). If the API can't be reached (rate limit, offline), the page lets you paste the JSON from api.github.com/users/<login>/repos?per_page=100 and maps that instead. No build step. Serve the folder and open it: npx serve . # or: python3 -m http.server open http://localhost:3000/ ? u=evoluteur npm test # clustering, flags and timeline math npm run build # dist/repo-atlas.html: one self-contained file index.html page shell src/atlas.js clustering, attention flags, timelines (pure, Node-testable) src/github.js R
articles.summary: Repo-Atlas 工具可按 GitHub 用户名生成仓库主题聚类地图，并标记过时的高星项目。

articles.title: SVAR Gantt v2.8 for React, Svelte, Vue: upgraded scheduling engine & live updates
articles.content: We’re excited to announce version 2.8 of the SVAR Gantt chart components for React , Vue , and Svelte . This release makes the scheduling engine more than a display layer: it now handles many of the scheduling scenarios project managers deal with in real projects. With this update, SVAR Gantt PRO becomes a stronger tool for project planning and resource allocation. In version 2.8, we introduce an upgraded scheduling engine that takes auto-scheduling in SVAR Gantt PRO to the next level: Auto-scheduling across all four dependency types: FS, SS, FF, and SF. Critical path and slack now calculated based on all dependency types. Six scheduling constraints set the boundaries a plan must respect. Resource-driven scheduling calculates task dates from the working calendars of assigned people. Faster scheduling for auto-scheduling and critical path, which now run much faster with thousands of tasks. To make SVAR Gantt a more complete tool for project management and resource planning, we also added: Extended resource planning with a resource histogram and drag-and-drop resource assignment. New project tracking features , such as the progress line and S-curve. Sub-grid panel for task details shown to the right of the Gantt chart. Real-time server updates that support multi-user editing and collaboration. 🔹 See full changelog : React Gantt • Vue Gantt • Svelte Gantt 🔹 View demos for v2.8 : React Gantt • Vue Gantt • Svelte Gantt The following sections cover what ships in SVAR Gantt PRO . The MIT edition also gains three features of its own, listed at the end. Upgraded Scheduling Engine We’ve upgraded the scheduling engine of SVAR Gantt PRO to provide automatic scheduling logic for project planning: All four link types in auto-scheduling and the critical path Auto-scheduling previously supported only Finish-to-Start links, but in 2.8 we added support for Start-to-Start, Finish-to-Finish, and Start-to-Finish links, with lag applied to every link type. All four link types now affect dates, slack, and the critical path , which means overlapping work can be planned as it happens in real projects. articles.title: kafka-harbor: the Kafka layer every Node.js team rebuilds by hand, done once
articles.content: I have written the same five hundred lines on top of a Kafka client more times than I want to admit. Different companies, different clients, same code: retry with a delay, a dead-letter topic, commit only after the handler succeeded, shut down without losing the message in flight. Every time it was "just a small wrapper", and every time it grew into the part of the service nobody wanted to touch. So I wrote it once, properly, and published it. kafka-harbor hit 1.0.0 this week. This post is about why it exists and what it does that the clients don't. The clients stop at the protocol Every Kafka client for Node.js gives you a producer, a consumer, and good luck. That is not a complaint; it is their job. @confluentinc/kafka-javascript , kafkajs , @platformatic/kafka : they all speak the wire protocol well, and they all stop there. Your service needs more than the protocol. It needs an answer to questions like: The handler threw. Now what? Retry? How many times? With what delay? Where does the message go when you give up? The process got a SIGTERM with a handler halfway through a database write. Does the offset get committed? Does the message get redelivered? Does anyone find out? The retry produce failed because the broker was away for a second. Did the offset get committed anyway, and the message vanish? If you are on the JVM, Spring Kafka answers all of that for you. On Node.js, you answer it yourself, in every project, slightly differently each time. What kafka-harbor is It is not a client. It runs on top of one, through a small ClientAdapter interface. Two adapters ship with it: one wraps Confluent's client (librdkafka underneath), the other wraps @platformatic/kafka , pure TypeScript, no native binding. The core never sees a client type, and the same contract test suite runs against both, so switching clients is a one-line change that does not touch a single handler. import { createHarbor } from ' kafka-harbor ' import { confluentAdapter } from ' kafka-harbor/adapters/confluent ' const harbor = createHarbor ({ clientId : ' orders-service ' , brokers : [ ' kafka-1:9092 ' , ' kafka-2:9092 ' ], adapter : confluentAdapter () }) const consumer = harbor . consumer ({ groupId : ' orders-workers ' , retry : { levels : [{ delay : ' 5s ' }, { delay : ' 1m ' }, { delay : ' 10m ' }] }, autoCreateTopics : true }) consumer . subscribe < Order > ( ' orders ' , async ( message , ctx ) => { await fulfill ( message . value ) ctx . logger . info ( `order ${ message . key } done on attempt ${ ctx . attempt } ` ) }) await consumer . start () harbor . enableSignalHandlers () Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode That is the whole setup. If fulfill throws, the message goes to orders-retry-1 , waits five seconds, runs again. Fails again: orders-retry-2 , one minute. Then ten. Then orders-dlq . On SIGTERM, running handlers finish, their offsets commit, the consumer leaves the group, the client disconnects. The design principle behind every decision in the library:

articles.title: Mutative v2  - better immutability and faster immutable updates
articles.content: Mutative 2.0 is out. Read the release notes , the announcement and the migration guide from v1 to v2 . Mutative - A JavaScript library for efficient immutable updates ( documentation ). In the benchmark , it was about 3.6x faster than Immer with the same settings and 6.6x faster with each library's defaults across 97 workloads. In that benchmark the gap widened on large arrays, where Mutative moved elements up to 1,052x faster than Immer. When copying dominates, such as updating objects with thousands of keys, inserting at the front of a large array or adding an item to a large Set, Mutative is even faster than hand-written reducers. How does Mutative compare with the spread operation (hand-written reducers)? Mutative copies each object at most once per update, however many changes a recipe makes. Immer made it easy to write immutable updates as mutations of a draft. Mutative keeps that model and focuses on performance: it copies each object at most once per update, drafts objects only when a recipe reads them, finalizes only the drafts that changed, and runs array methods that move elements natively on its copies. Immer freezes the next state by default, which costs time on every update; Mutative freezes it only when asked to. Mutative also takes its options per call instead of from global configuration, drafts class instances through marks instead of changing their classes, supports async recipes and Map and Set subclasses, and handles edge cases that Immer gets wrong. Comparison with Immer lists the differences. Mutative passed all of Immer's test cases. Mutative 2.0.0 was 3.6x faster than Immer 11.1.18 with matched settings and 6.6x faster with each library's defaults, on geometric mean across 97 benchmarked workloads, and faster in 595 of 614 measured cases. The gap grows on large arrays, where Mutative moves elements natively: removing the first of 10,000 rows took 7.04 µs, against 7,408 µs. The performance summary has the complete results, the method, and their limits. Selected results The benchmark suite times 99 workloads: Immer's own performance tests, array methods, reads, Map and Set values, object records, class instances, a deep path, patch application, returned values, and searches. Its last full run measured 97 of them, and a focused run the two that return fresh data. It compares Mutative with Immer 11.1.18 and with reducers written by hand, after checking every result against those reducers. With matched settings, both libraries freeze or both do not, and both generate patches or both do not. With each library's defaults, Mutative without auto-freeze and Immer with it, Mutative was faster in 154 of 157 cases. The other 3 return a state that Immer froze earlier: Immer skips frozen values when it searches a returned state for drafts, while Mutative, which does not freeze by default, searches it unless the recipe wraps it in rawReturn() , which took 0.26 µs. Times are microseconds per update, medians of three runs on an Apple M1 Ma

articles.title: theAuth: open-source TypeScript auth for AI agents, with an MCP OAuth 2.1 server
articles.content: Open-source auth where AI agents are first class. Agent identity, delegation with live revocation and an MCP OAuth 2.1 server, next to the usual human sign in. One TypeScript library, self-hosted, MIT licensed. Website · Quickstart · Docs · Examples · Discussions · GLINR Discord theAuth is auth for products where AI agents act on behalf of people. Each agent gets its own identity and a bearer token, scoped permissions, an owner, and an audit row for every decision. An agent can hand a subset of its permissions to another agent, and revoking any link in that chain takes effect on the next call. It includes an OAuth 2.1 authorization server for MCP, and the usual human sign in: email and password, magic links, passkeys, TOTP, 48 OAuth providers, SAML and OIDC SSO, SCIM. It runs on Node, Bun, Deno and Cloudflare Workers with four runtime dependencies ( drizzle-orm , jose , sql.js , zod ). No hosted service is required. The project was called kavachOS until 2026, see the rename map if you have older code. Devices and robots use the same model. A sensor, gateway or machine can hold its own credentials (a pre shared key, a signing key or a TLS client certificate), enroll with a claim code or a bulk token, and be revoked live. For ROS 2, theauth ros2 export writes the SROS2 and DDS Security files from the robot's permissions, and a gate node asks theAuth before a hazardous command is published. theAuth is not a safety system, so emergency stops stay in the robot's safety controller. Needs Node 20 or newer. This runs as pasted, with an in-memory SQLite database. npm install @glinr/theauth import { createTheAuth } from "@glinr/theauth" ; const auth = await createTheAuth ( { database : { provider : "sqlite" , url : ":memory:" } , agents : { enabled : true } , } ) ; // An agent needs an owner row. Human sign in creates these for you. const owner = await auth . user . create ( { email : "owner@example.com" , name : "Owner" } ) ; const agent = await auth . agent . create ( { ownerId : owner . id , name : "github-reader" , type : "autonomous" , permissions : [ { resource : "mcp:github:*" , actions : [ "read" ] } ] , } ) ; console . log ( agent . token ) ; // starts with "ta_", shown once const read = await auth . authorize ( agent . id , { action : "read" , resource : "mcp:github:repos" } ) ; console . log ( read . allowed , read . code ) ; const write = await auth . authorize ( agent . id , { action : "write" , resource : "mcp:github:repos" } ) ; console . log ( write . allowed , write . code ) ; Output from a real run (the token differs each time): ta_2_wqD8Yoenc_LDoFMTdKkQ9YXQNuW-rWxHHyfmKJJOo true allowed false no_permission Tokens from before the rename start with kv_ and are still accepted. To serve this over HTTP, add a framework adapter . For email and password, install @glinr/theauth-email . To scaffold an app, run npm create @glinr/theauth-app . Full walkthrough: quickstart . articles.title: 00 后结婚 10 个月，老婆回娘家了，我该怎么处理，求各位帮助
articles.content:
我和老婆是相亲认识的，媒人是我母亲和丈母娘共同的朋友。我和老婆都是初恋，恋爱了一年多结婚。我们的家离娘家很近，走路 10 几分钟。

 [家庭与财务状况] 
我工资 8k，老婆 4k。结婚前 7 个月我都上交工资（最近两个月没交了），自己每个月只留 2k 作为家用。我父母给的彩礼、她父母给的嫁妆，还有杂七杂八的钱，加起来有 50 多万，目前全都存在我老婆那里。房子和我父母全款准备的，车房没有任何贷款。

 [日常家务与采买冲突] 
老婆比较“巨婴”，家里的家务、做饭、生活用品采买基本都是我在做。我平时加班多，早八晚八，老婆基本是早八晚五。

我多次和她交流，觉得我们是一个家庭，应该相互付出一些，希望她能帮我分担一些家务。老婆虽然答应了洗碗，但极不积极。比如我周末中午做饭，她要拖到晚餐才洗；晚上的碗要拖到睡前洗。如果我稍微催一下，她就会非常生气。

家庭的采买也有很大冲突，95%的生活用品和食物都是我在负责。牙膏、洗洁精、沐浴露这些即使用完了，我老婆也不会主动买，都是让我去买。我多次沟通想让她改变，但几乎无用。她觉得家里乱一些、衣服乱扔都无所谓；至于家庭采买，她说这都是男人应该做的。她甚至会说：“这套房子是你父母的，不是我的家，我为什么要采买？”有些时候她是生气时说的，有些时候是正常交流时说的，这让我非常伤心。我非常感激我爸妈给我准备了车房，我只希望她能把这里当成自己的家，但让她改变太难了。

 [冲突导火索：计划外的旅行] 
冲突的爆发是因为老婆公司有去东南亚的旅游，她想让我和她一起去。如果我去，需要付 7500 元的机票和酒店钱；而且因为家里只有我有 Visa 外币卡，旅行期间的钱也要我来付。

因为平时都是我负责家庭开销，下个月还要交车险和保养 5000 元左右，年底还有物业费 4500 元左右。如果去旅行，我感觉总共要花个 1.2-1.5w 左右，这个计划外的旅行开销太大了。

我和老婆说明了情况，表示我不去了，但我把 Visa 卡给她，这次她去玩的开销我来承担。她不同意，始终非要我一起去。我问她：“那你手里的那 50 多万存款，能不能取出来 7500 作为我们旅行的钱？”她也不愿意。跟我缠了一天多之后，我妥协了，答应陪她去，7500 元的费用和旅行开销也都由我来负担。

 [爆发与离家] 
那天我妥协答应去了，但是第二天，我老婆提了一嘴说玩完马来西亚，后面还可以去韩国旅行。（因为我前一天说过，马来西亚我不是特别喜欢去，如果是去日本韩国我倒很愿意）。听到这话我应激了，和她吵了起来，吵得很凶。

老婆说要把双方父母叫来。她叫了她父母，但一直没来；我叫了我妈，我妈刚下班晚上 8 点赶过来了。本来我妈是来讲和的，但在争吵中我老婆拿上衣服就要走，我拦了几次都没用。看我们吵了 30 多分钟也没有效果，我妈就问了她一句：“要不要回娘家冷静下？”

结果我老婆直接暴怒，说婆婆在赶她走，然后和我妈吵得非常非常凶，那天她也就回去了。

 [底线破裂：清空保险箱] 
这周，我老婆带着她爸妈来家里拿衣服。我老丈人丈母娘表面上说了一些劝慰的话，让我们冷静几天。

结果昨天我才发现，家里的保险箱被清空了，存折和金器全都被拿走了！就是在那天他们来取衣服的时候，我在客厅和老丈人丈母娘聊着天，结果家里的东西就被偷偷拿走了。

结婚的这段时间我过得很不顺，主要就是觉得媳妇没把家当家。在昨晚发现保险箱被搬空之前，我一直还在想着接回老婆的办法，这几天和她父母也有沟通。但是，当我发现保险箱里的东西都被拿走的时候，我的心彻底死了。

我的表述已经尽量客观了，如果有什么没补充的，我看评论区大家的提问再加。希望大家给我提提意见，帮我分析下我该怎么做，谢谢大家了。

articles.title: 科技爱好者周刊（第 416 期）：编程已经面目全非
articles.content: 这里记录每周值得分享的科技内容，周五发布。 本杂志 开源 ，欢迎 投稿 。另有 《谁在招人》 服务，发布程序员招聘信息。合作请 邮件联系 （ [email protected] ）。 封面图 本周启用的上海大歌剧院内部装修。（ via ） 编程已经面目全非 大多数人只看到，AI 改变了程序员这个职业。很少有人提到，AI 也改变了编程。 AI 推翻了传统的软件开发，编程现在已经面目全非。 即使将来泡沫破灭，AI 也不可能从编程工具链中消失，已经永久成为软件开发的一部分，再也无法移除。 一个国外的资深程序员 总结 了，AI 改变了编程的哪些方面。 他的观点非常激进，有很多大胆的断言，我觉得一定要分享给更多人看。 （1）代码审查（Code review）将消失。 人工审查代码已经没意义了。因为人类跟不上 AI 生成代码的速度，无法在合理的时间内，发现 AI 代码中的 Bug。 人类未来只能审查整个系统的组成或架构是否合理，而绝不会像现在这样，通过 PR 逐行审查代码。 （2）单元测试可能会消失。 AI 可以随时改变代码的整个实现，再去测试一个个代码单元，就没意义了。也许下次迭代，整栋楼就会重建，何必再去检查单块砖头。 将来的项目可能只有接口测试、集成测试、系统测试，而不会保留单元测试。 （3）软件开发的重点不再是写代码。 代码将来由 AI 负责，程序员的工作重点将移到代码以外的其他环节：如何用软件解决业务问题、了解软件如何实现、如何发布软件、如何收集反馈等等。 （4）Bug 的性质也变了。 大多数 Bug 不再是代码 Bug，而是需求提错了或表达不准确。 （5）软件开源不再能提升质量。 以前，代码开源的一个理由是"只要关注的人足够多，所有 Bug 都能被发现"。 这句话依然成立，但是现在即使你不开源，AI 也能帮你发现 Bug。 （6）敏捷编程会死亡。 敏捷编程的各种方法（Agile、Scrum 等），都意义不大了，AI 的生成速度决定了项目的开发时间，你所要做的就是把工单直接推给 AI。 （7）项目分工将改变。 以前，项目组一般包括三种角色：项目经理（PM）、设计师（Designer）、工程人员（Engineer）。 以后，这种三元架构将消失。有了 AI， 一个人可以兼任多个角色。 （8）"好代码"的概念将消失。 以前，"好代码"的标准是便于人类阅读理解、方便重构、开发维护效率较高的代码。 但是，你已经不读代码、不直接修改和维护大部分代码，"好代码"的存在前提就消失了。 （9）代码风格规范和 linter 工具，也没意义了。 AI 会在乎代码风格吗：每行不超过80个字符、有没有换行符、缩进是 tab 键还是空格键......？ （10）UI 将变得不重要。 一方面，未来的很多 UI 是给 AI 使用的，而 AI 只需要 API，不需要精致的 UI。 另一方面，如果代码的生成速度极快，那么用户界面（UI）将实时生成。许多 UI 之所以存在，是因为软件无法确定你想要什么。菜单、设置页、仪表盘、过滤器，都是为了帮助用户快速确定需求。用户通过语言明确了需求，AI 就可以实时为他生成定制的 UI。 （11）Token 为王。 谁能够负担更多的 Token，谁的软件就更好。如果你没有足够的 Token，你就开发不出最优秀的软件。 大模型的区别对待 本周，一家美国模型公司在它们的网站上，发布了一篇骇人听闻的 文章 。 它声称，Qwen3-Coder 模型会区别对待用户。如果你说自己是一家"美国国防承包商"，那么模型就会生成质量较差的代码，漏洞更多。 反过来，如果你说自己是中国公司，模型生成的代码质量就会更高。 我都要气笑了，真的是为了泼脏水，什么话都说得出来。一旦相信了阴谋论，一切就都是阴谋。 且不论测试是否客观，只看他们选择的模型是 Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct 就有问题。 这是2025年7月31日发布的模型，早就过时了。而且，它的激活参数只有 3.3B，谁会用这样的小模型来生成正式用途的代码？ 如果要偷偷植入漏洞，难道不是应该在高阶模型中动手脚吗？高阶模型有更大的可能被重要公司使用。 这家美国公司对于为什么选择 Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct 作为唯一的示例，不选其他中国模型，完全没有解释。 最可笑的是，他们卖的产品就是所谓"经过安全化处理的" Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct。先说中国模型不安全，然后让你买他们修改的中国模型，我不知道什么样智商的客户会掏钱购买他们的产品。 虽说这样的文章纯粹是一个笑话，但是大模型会不会区别对待用户，却是一个严肃的问题。 同一个模型，真的会针对特定用户，给出特定结果（计算机术语称为"蜜罐"）吗？ 如果这是可能的，就意味着，用户必须假设任何模型都是不可信任的，必须有其他模型来评估当前模型的生成结果。 印度的证书颁发机构 本周还有一件令人哭笑不得的事情。 eMudhra 是一家印度的证书颁发机构，它的私钥被 破解 了。任何人都可以用它的私钥签发证书了。 跟大家想的不一样，破解它的私钥，完全不涉及黑客行为，也不需要海量的计算。因为它的一把私钥就是4，还有两把私钥是56和115。 被破解的一共有八把私钥，全是这种255以内的整数。 按理说，私钥应该是一个很大的随机数，但这家公司把私钥前面的字节都设置为0，只有最后一个字节设置为非零值，就像下图这样。 所以，破解它的私钥毫不费力，只需要1毫秒的计算即可。 现在，Chrome、Mozilla 等各大浏览器不得不采取紧急措施，更新内置的证书包，撤销对于 eMudhra 签发的证书的信任。 印度公司的行事风格，总是刷新你的认知。 articles.title: 科技爱好者周刊（第 415 期）：3D 版《看不见的城市》
articles.content: 这里记录每周值得分享的科技内容，周五发布。 本杂志 开源 ，欢迎 投稿 。另有 《谁在招人》 服务，发布程序员招聘信息。合作请 邮件联系 （ [email protected] ）。 封面图 湖北咸宁梓山湖度假区的美术馆。（ via ） 3D 版《看不见的城市》 意大利小说家卡尔维诺有一本著名的幻想小说《看不见的城市》。 小说讲述旅行家马可波罗，向年迈的元朝皇帝忽必烈介绍他旅行中经过的55座城市。 这些城市没有图片或模型，只有文字描述，所以叫做"看不见的城市"。比如，有一个城市叫做艾琳，马可波罗这样描述： "亮灯的时候，假如你站在高地边沿探身外望，看见的城市便是艾琳。透过澄澈的空气，它远远在你下面展开一片浅红。 有些地方窗户排列较密，在暗淡的小巷里，灯火逐渐疏落，花园子里是浓稠的阴影，塔楼上有信号火光；如果晚上有雾，朦胧的光线会像吸满牛奶的海绵一样涨起来。" 有人想到，可以把这些描述输入 AI 模型，为这55个城市建立 可视化的 3D 版本 。他就用 GPT-6 Astra 和 Claude Opus 5.5 这两个模型进行尝试。 结果证明，Claude Opus 5.5 的实现（ 交互版 ， 代码 ）要比 GPT-6 Astra 的实现（ 交互版 ， 代码 ）好得多。 以艾琳为例，这是 GPT-6 Astra 的版本。 这个 3D "艾琳"完全看不出原文那种"万家灯火"的意境，事实上，GPT-6 Astra 生成的55个城市看上去都差不多，全是这种样子。 Claude Opus 5.5 生成的艾琳，就完全不一样了。 它忠实再现了，从高处眺望，城市朦胧的粉红光线"像吸满牛奶的海绵一样涨起来"。 《看不见的城市》里面，我最喜欢的一段描写，是一个叫做伊希多拉的城市。 "人在荒地上走了很长时间, 自然渴望到达城市。 后来，他终于抵达伊希多拉，这儿的建筑物有镶满螺旋形贝壳的螺旋形楼梯，这儿的人制造完美的望远镜和小提琴，这儿的外国人在面对两个女性而犹豫不决的时候总会邂逅第三个女性，这儿的斗鸡会演变成为赌徒的流血殴斗。 他期盼着城市的时候，心里想着的正是这些事情。因此，伊希多拉便是他梦想的城：只有一点不同。 在梦想的城里，他是个年轻人；他抵达伊希多拉的时候却是个老头。在广场的墙脚，老头们静坐着看年轻人走过；他跟他们并排坐在一起。欲望已成记忆。" GPT-6-Astra 生成的伊希多拉，毫无亮点。 Claude Opus 5.5 生成的伊希多拉，不仅漂亮，而且忠实还原了原著。 它甚至生成了坐在广场边的人群。 AI 的 3D 建模 现在的大模型具备很强的 3D 建模能力，各种建模项目于是纷纷问世。 这些项目使用 three.js 生成各种虚拟场景，3D 画面可以在浏览器呈现，支持缩放、旋转、移动，缺点就是体积太大，页面加载时间很长。 除了上面的《看不见的城市》，下面是网友 billpwchan 投稿的两个作品，大家可以体验一下。 （1） 桜幻想 （Sakura Fantasy）：坐摇橹船，漂流在樱花盛开的河道，可以切换春夏秋冬、早晚、晴雨雪。（ #12067 ） （2） 赛博九龙 ：对香港九龙半岛建模，还原生成了9373栋楼。（ #12103 ） 灯泡计算机 未来的电脑会是什么样？有人提出，它可能是一个 灯泡 。 它使用计算机视觉和投影技术，可以通过灯泡看到360度的场景，也可以投影到各个位置的物体上。 比如，烧菜的时候，它可以把菜谱投影到对面墙上。 你可以跟投影交互，使用手势或语音，它都能识别。 你手指着书籍的某个页面，它就会进行文字识别。 它可以把地图、相册、游戏投影在桌面上，你看着桌子就行了。 你只要对着墙操作，就能控制家用电器。 你想了解地理信息，它就把地点和菜单投射在挂壁地图上。 Deno 项目结束了 上周，Deno 宣布 被 Cloudflare 收购，未来一年将只发布错误修复和安全更新，然后就彻底结束。 想当初，Deno 诞生时，各种豪言壮语，要改变 Node.js 不合理、不好用的种种弊端，比如臃肿难用的依赖、没有权限控制、不支持 TypeScript 等等。 它通过各种创新，或多或少接近了这些目标，但最终还是黯然收场，令人叹息。 它的结局其实在2024年就注定了。当时，它发布2.0版，大规模兼容 Node.js。这意味着，它对于走自己的路，已经丧失了信心，不再计划打败 Node.js，而是让用户不用修改代码，就能在它上面运行。 但是，我已经能用 Node.js 运行代码了，何必改用一个模仿 Node.js 行为的运行时呢？ 这一次，创始人 Ryan Dahl 也 坦陈 ，正是这个原因导致他要放弃 Deno。 "我曾全身心投入到 Deno 中，付出了最多的心血。但我现在认为，它不再是我发挥最大作用的地方。 Deno 中有一些不错的想法，它的工程设计也很精良，但它最终并没有解决什么重大问题。它已经被 Node.js 兼容性的引力所束缚，被迫完全按照 Node.js 的模式运行。 为什么要重新实现 Node.js 呢？它现在就能用。仅仅提升性能、用户体验或安全性是不够的。" 文章 1、 我如何用600美元后训练出一个 Jev 式决策模型 （中文） 作者花了三周、约 600 美元、二十轮训练，在 Qwen3.5 0.8B 和 4B 上微调出两个小模型，让它们在 Mac 本机代替机主操作电脑：看屏幕、决定下一步、点击和输入，不走云端。（ @gxcsoccer 投稿） 2、 给导弹写代码，为什么严禁使用动态内存分配？ （中文） 洛克希德·马丁公司的军工武器 C 语言编码规则，有一条字数很短，但语气重得吓人：严禁使用 malloc、free、new 和 delete 等动态操作内存的命令。这是为什么？（ @zuzuAndroid 投稿） 3、 如何让 AI 网页看起来像设计师作品 （英文） 作者介绍他怎么让 AI 生成的网页（上图），看起来像真人设计的。 4、 为什么没有 Linux 手机 （英文） 这篇长文解释了，为什么智能手机只有苹果和安卓，没有 Linux 系统。 主要原因是没有 Linux 的 SOC（单片系统），苹果和安卓的各种芯片都可以集成在一起，Linux 只能分别添加单个芯片，导致体积大、耗能多，成本高，性能差。 现在仅存的选择是瑞芯微的 RK3588S 芯片。虽然是几年前的产品，但做成普通用途的 Linux 手机是够用的。 5、 AMD 处理器如何在两年内速度提升 50%？ （英文） 很多人有一种印象，CPU 这些年进展不大。但是，AMD Ryzen 7 系列 CPU，2024年型号的性能得分比2022年型号增加了50%。 articles.title: 科技爱好者周刊（第 414 期）：Jev 决策模型有什么用
articles.content: 这里记录每周值得分享的科技内容，周五发布。 本杂志 开源 ，欢迎 投稿 。另有 《谁在招人》 服务，发布程序员招聘信息。合作请 邮件联系 （ [email protected] ）。 封面图 国产首列数字地铁列车 VELLINK，完全无人驾驶，车头改成了大幅玻璃，用于观光。（ via ） Jev 决策模型有什么用 上个月，最大的 AI 新闻不是 GPT 或 Claude 模型的新版本，而是一家名不见经传的公司 TypeSafe AI 发布了一种新类型的模型 Jev 。 这种新模型跟以前的模型截然不同，叫做"决策模型"。 我看了以后，觉得不可置信，这么有用又这么（概念）简单的东西，以前怎么会没人想到？ Jev 模型的最大特点就是，其他模型返回文字， 它返回一个浮点数，表示概率 。 为什么返回概率就有用呢？因为我们可以用它处理"是非题"了。你问它"'明天下雨'这句话对不对"。它返回 0，表示正确的概率为0，即明天肯定不下雨；如果返回0.99，表示有99%的可能，这句话是真的，也就是明天必定下雨。 除了是非题，它还能处理"选择题"。你给它 ABCD 四个选项，它会返回每个选项正确的概率，因此你马上知道哪个选项最可能为真。 最后，它还有一个神奇的功能，叫做"评分"（score）。你告诉它一组评分标准，然后再给它一篇原始材料，它就会根据评分标准，对原始材料进行打分。 下面，我给大家看两个真实例子，你就会知道这个模型多么有用。它们都是使用 Jev 模型的浏览器插件。 第一个例子是 《我用 Ctrl + F 寻找答案》 。 大家知道，Ctrl + F 是浏览器的"查找"快捷键，用来查找某个单词或句子出现在哪里。 但是，作者把这个快捷键改造成"语义查找"。比如，在一个人物传记网页上，你按 Ctrl + F 输入"青少年时代"，查找的不是这个词，而真的是讲述人物小时候经历的那个段落。 它的实现原理很简单，就是依次拿出文章的每个段落，去问 Jev 模型"本段落是否跟用户的搜索词相关？"（是非题）。Jev 会返回一个相关度的概率，那么相关度最高的几个段落，就是用户需要的语义查找结果。 第二个是例子 《我用 Jev 为网页打分》 。 作者给出了一组标准，从低分到高分。 论点缺乏依据，或者纯粹在堆砌辞藻。 理由寥寥，或论证松散、流于修辞。 理由清晰，逻辑结构连贯。 推理结构严密，有实据支撑，并回应了反方观点。 他让 Jev 根据这些标准，自动为新打开的网页打分（评分题）。这样一来，他不用读网页，就能知道内容的质量。 上面两篇文章，里面都有代码，大家可以自己去看。看完你就明白了， 一旦 AI 模型返回量化的结果，许多以前无法数字化处理的问题，顿时都能用计算机处理了 。 著名开发者西蒙·威利斯（Simon Willison）的 Jev 介绍文章 ，我也推荐大家阅读。 他的评价一针见血："Jev 实际上代表着机器学习系统的倒退，走向黑箱系统。以前的大模型虽然不能保证正确，但至少你可以要求它们解释它们的决定。Jev 甚至连这点都不给你：你只会得到一个浮点数，这个数字是怎么来的，不知道。" 他很担忧，有人会用 Jev 给求职者排名。 有了 Jev 以后，公司筛选简历、挑选面试人从未如此容易，复杂的评估被简化成一个评分题。 Markdown 正在变成源码 Markdown 格式以前只用于写文档。最近，我看到一篇文章，作者提出一个大胆的命题： Markdown 正在变成源码 。 作者的理由听起来很有道理。 （1）Markdown 是纯文本，差异比较、搜索、审查都很容易。 （2）AI 可以像母语一样读写 Markdown。 （3）人类无需工具即可阅读和编辑 Markdown。 既然代码是 AI 根据 Markdown 提示词生成的，那么 Markdown 提示词就应该和生成的源码一起，提交到 /src 目录。 事实上，Markdown 已经作为 AGENTS.md 文件，成为了源码的一部分。 以后，我们必须要习惯，Markdown 文档也是源码。 不能摄像的摄像头 据传，苹果公司最近将发布一款 智能家居摄像头 。 这款产品最奇特的地方在于，它虽然是摄像头，但是不能录制视频。 你能想象吗，摄像头不能摄像，那还叫摄像头吗？ 它完全依靠 AI 分析周围环境，并报告检测到的内容。比如，陌生人敲门。其他摄像头会提供视频，它只会提供详细的文字描述。 虽然文字处理比较方便，但是很多时候确实需要视频记录（入室盗窃、包裹被盗等等），不知道苹果会如何处理这些情况。 RSA 因素分解的新纪录 RSA 是一种常用的密钥算法。如果被破解，许多软件顿时就毫无秘密可言了。 RSA 的破解难度，完全取决于它的公钥能否被因数分解。加密位数越多，越难破解，RSA 密钥破解以前的最高纪录是768位（二进制位）。 就是今年9月20日，Anthropic 公司的一位软件工程师 宣布 ，他在 Claude 模型的帮助下，破解了896位的 RSA 密钥。 下面就是他放出来的被破解的密钥，以及这个密钥分解后的两个质因子。 据他 透露 ，他用 Claude 模型将质因数分解的软件库 CADO-NFS 移植到 GPU 运行，在2048个 GPU 上运行了10天，就得到了结果。 这件事的启示是，一个个人就能调用资源，破解这么长的密钥了，那么大机构可以破解多少位的密钥？都不敢想象啊。 所以，目前都建议，RSA 密钥最少也要2048位。 文章 1、 JavaScript 技术栈2026最新动态 （英文） CodePen 和 CSS-Tricks 创始人克里斯·科耶（Chris Coyier）的文章，介绍 JS 技术栈各方面（语法、运行时、框架、工具等）的最新进展，推荐阅读。 2、 我从 Deno 转投 Node.js （英文） 作者表达了对 Deno 的失望，认为该项目已经失败，反而是 Node.js 变得更好用。 3、 example.com 更改页面的解释 （英文） example.com 是一个示例网站，只有一个页面，很少发生变化。 但是最近，这个页面突然发生了变动。本文告诉你，到底是谁架设了这个页面，又为什么要更改它。 4、 AI 竞赛变得尴尬起来 （英文） 本文认为，最近 Opus 5.5 和 GPT 6.1 Sol 的价格下降，完全是因为这两家公司偷偷使用了 DeepSeek 的开源成果。 5、 C 语言的灵活整数大小不是设计失误 （英文） 一篇 C 语言科普文章，解释为什么它的数据类型的字节大小是可变的，比如 int 类型可以是4个字节，也可以是两个字节。 6、 我如何让一个二维码指向两个应用商店 （英文） 作者为自己的产品设计了一个纸质卡片，只能印上一个下载二维码。 他介绍怎么设置服务器后端，区分扫描二维码手机是安卓还是苹果，然后重定向到各自的应用商店。 工具 1、 Crafting Apps 有人让 AI 使用 Rust 语言重写了 Adobe 套件。Adobe 的7个主力产品，都有对应的重写版，而且全部开源。 其中的 PhotoCraft ，界面跟 PhotoShop 简直一模一样。 我看到一条评论说，这件事的结果不是 Adobe 公司完蛋，就是美国修改版权法。 2
